intended_object: This is the action of the sign group ∏_{i∈ℕ} {±1} on ℤ through its i-th factor: (ε, n) ↦ ε_i·n. It is the coordinate piece of the coordinatewise sign action on ℤ^ℕ. I took this from the docstring and from how it is used in `product_action_coordinate`, part of the module's counterexample about infinite products of discrete modules (Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg I §1.1).
explanation:
The body is `(actor index) • value`. Here `actor : ℕ → ℤˣ` and `•` is the standard action of `ℤˣ` on `ℤ`, which is multiplication by ±1. So the definition evaluates ε at coordinate i and multiplies n by ε_i, exactly as the docstring says.

The file proves by `rfl` (`product_action_coordinate`) that the Pi action of `SignGroup` on `ℕ → ℤ` is this map applied coordinate by coordinate, which confirms it is the intended piece of the product action.

The object is a specific action used in a specific counterexample: the countable product of `ℤˣ` acting on copies of `ℤ`. Its specificity is the content of the example, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has the general Pi action, but not this coordinate map as a named declaration; it is just the pullback of `Units` acting on `ℤ` along evaluation at i. There are no degenerate cases that could make it go wrong.
